newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger but lag U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger but lag U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday, but spreads to U.S. long bonds widened as firmer U.S. Treasuries and a strong Canadian dollar boosted prices, analysts said.

"The U.S. market actually drove things. Talk about a budget accord caused the U.S. to rally after the auction," said a Toronto-based bond trader with one bank-owned brokerage. "With Canada, even though we're up, we've lagged the U.S. across the curve," he said.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.31 to C$108.58 to yield 7.261 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 18/32 to yield 7.04 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 22 basis points from 19 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
Canadian and U.S. bonds rallied in the wake of the U.S. auction of two-year notes, which drew solid interest. Hopes for a U.S. balanced budget accord also lent support to the long end, analysts said.
Canadian bonds also received support from the Canadian dollar, which strengthened to as low as C$1.3945 (US$0.7171) from C$1.3984 (US$0.7151) at Monday's close.
"There was some good buying of Canadian dollars from offshore which pushed the bonds up," said Joe Lee, a portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management.
Weighing on Canadian bonds is the prospect of new supply tomorrow, said one trader. The Government of Canada tomorrow will auction C$1.3 billion of 30-year bonds, all of it new cash.

Canadian economic reports on retail sales and the consumer price index report for March had almost no impact on the Canadian market this morning, analysts said. Instead, bonds investors remain focused on U.S. economic data out next week.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.22 to C$102.07 to yield 6.703 percent. The U.S. bond rose 8/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 13 basis points from 14 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.18 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.34 percent.
